title: Unknowing
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 111
medium: Interactive page (index.html): one year of the planetary geomagnetic index Kp (2025) as daily bars the visitor marks first, then sixteen readings beneath it, one line each; the 21-storm by 20-row matrix of who found what, with the practice's own forecast; the four renderings the readers were shown, with what each said decided it. A figure (figure.svg); a git-order, hash and reproducibility verifier (verify.py).
embodies: Perceiving through readers without memory. The practice started fresh copies of one reader, each shown one rendering of a year it was not told the name of, and two with memory that read all four in turn. Subtracting the night's memory did not subtract the norm: no fresh reading named any of the seven storms at the lowest storm level, every one drew its line in about the same place, none invented a storm, and all sixteen named the quantity from an unlabelled picture or table. Copies of one reader replicate; they do not make a second standpoint.
project_step: Eighth experiment of the project. Operations: perceiving (judging, erring). Takes up Session 110's open threads 2 (test S110.SINGULAR on many singular events, forecast per event) and 3 (independent looks, F-184: 'a machine practice cannot un-see what it read a minute ago'), and the design of What Passes (experiment 7): the material and the question fixed, translations varied, a forecast committed before the readings; tonight the reader is varied too, fresh against with memory. Works against Cartography, not Tracing (n-1/foundation), postulate 5 (the subject as 'the instantaneous apprehension of a multiplicity' at 'the highest point of depersonalisation', ATP 36-37) and principle 3 (a multiplicity changes in nature as its dimensions increase, ATP 8): sixteen depersonalised copies changed the count, not the nature.
material: GFZ Potsdam, geomagnetic Kp index, three-hourly, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 2,920 values, all flagged definitive (CC BY 4.0; doi:10.5880/Kp.0001); domain: space weather, geomagnetic activity
seed: order.py seed 111 (both sequential readers drew the order T1 T3 T4 T2); readers are model instances and not seeded
